status: POST-HOC DIAGNOSTIC — NOT the declared primary statistic, and it cannot carry a claim
why: The declared primary was EVENT minus a matched NON-EVENT control, and one archetype (A18) survived Holm at 0.0484. But the CORPUS-LEVEL event-minus-control difference, which was computed in the same run and reported beside the ten, is -0.848pp at t -3.03 — statistically indistinguishable from A18's -0.809pp. So A18's survival is the corpus-wide 'a news day underperforms a quiet day in the same name-month' effect showing through a subset, not an archetype effect. This diagnostic asks the question that separates the two: is THIS archetype different from the OTHER EVENTS? It was computed after the results were read and is labelled post-hoc for that reason.
statistic: paired block difference, archetype events minus all other events, same blocks

family_correction.reading: SCREEN=BH-FDR admits a known false-discovery fraction and is for deciding what to look at next; EXPORT=Holm controls the family-wise error and is what a claim leaving this repository is judged by. `screened_not_exported` is the gap between 'worth another look' and 'defensible'.

verdict: ZERO of ten survive Holm and ZERO survive the BH-FDR screen; best Holm-adjusted p 0.544; not one archetype is powered for its own observed effect. The archetype partition carries no incremental information over 'an event happened' on this tape.

ar.reading: event minus the same names in the same months without the event; this is the number the hypothesis lives on

raw.reading: event minus the same names in the same months without the event; this is the number the hypothesis lives on

corpus_level_reference.reading: if this is non-zero, every archetype inherits it and the ten per-archetype differences are increments on top of it, not independent effects
